page: Microsoft Azure FX8ms_v2 is a compute- and memory-intensive virtual machine powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance exposes 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It integrates an unusually large memory allocation of 168.0 GB RAM, providing 21.0 GB of memory per vCPU, alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. Supported hardware extensions include AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8. The instance does not bundle local storage or dedicated graphics processing units, relying entirely on remote storage infrastructure.

Benchmark evaluations indicate exceptional single-thread processing capabilities driven by the 4.2 GHz clock frequency. The system achieved a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2362.0 and demonstrated top-decile text processing throughput, accompanied by strong single-threaded gzip compression at 34.9 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.5 GB/sec. Conversely, with an allocation capped at 8 vCPUs, aggregate multithreaded compute throughput remains average, yielding a multi-core Geekbench score of 8997.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 15770.47. In addition, while lightweight language model inference generates 291.75 tokens per second on a 135M model, performance drops significantly on 7B models due to the absence of hardware accelerators.

From an architectural standpoint, the FX8ms_v2 delivers an asymmetric resource profile tailored for workloads requiring strong per-core performance paired with large in-memory working sets rather than extensive horizontal thread scaling. The omission of bundled local storage necessitates attached premium storage for persistent or scratch volumes. This configuration fits electronic design automation (EDA), relational databases requiring high cache-to-core ratios, financial modeling, batch processing, and compilation workloads.
description: The Microsoft Azure FX8ms_v2 is an asymmetric cloud instance tailored for high-frequency, memory-dense workloads. Executing on Microsoft Hyper-V via a dedicated 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor, it provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, paired with 168.0 GB of system memory and 260 MB of L3 cache. Advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX are supported, while local storage and hardware GPUs are omitted. Benchmark metrics show top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2362.0 and strong compression throughput, though multi-core capabilities remain within mid-tier bounds. With a high ratio of 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, the instance offers significant memory density without requiring excessive core licensing. This makes the FX8ms_v2 well matched for electronic design automation (EDA), in-memory caching, software compilation, and financial modeling applications.
